arxiv-1612-07521.title: Projections of orbital measures for classical Lie groups
arxiv-1612-07521.description: Abstract 1. Introduction. Let G_{n} be a compact Lie group from the list: \mathrm{SO}(2n+1) , \mathrm{Sp}(2n), \mathrm{O}(2n) . Consider the adjoint action of G_{n} on its Lie algebra \mathfrak{g}_{n} . Since G_{n} is a compact group, for each orbit of the action there exists a unique G_{n} -invariant probability measure supported on this orbit.

arxiv-1902-07392.title: Optomechanical quadrature squeezing in the non-Markovian regime Journal: ol
arxiv-1902-07392.creator: Biao Xiong, Xun Li, Shi-Lei Chao, Ling Zhou
arxiv-1902-07392.description: Abstract Squeezing of quantum fluctuation plays an important role in fundamental quantum physics and has marked influence on ultrasensitive detection. We propose a scheme to generate and enhance the squeezing of mechanical mode by exposing the optomechanical system to a non-Markovian environment.

arxiv-2011-08645.title: The Origin of the Elements and Other Implications of Gravitational Wave Detection for Nuclear Physics Journal: EPJ Sciences 4Open
arxiv-2011-08645.creator: D. Lunney The wave that launched a thousand shifts
arxiv-2011-08645.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by D. Lunney The wave that launched a thousand shifts. The neutron-star collision revealed by the event GW170817 gave us a first glimpse of a possible birthplace of most of our heavy elements. The multi-messenger nature of this historical event combined gravitational waves, a gamma-ray burst and optical astronomy of a “kilonova,” bringing the first observations of rapid neutron capture ( r r process) nucleosynthesis after 60 years of speculation.

arxiv-2110-11618.title: Intelligent metaphotonics empowered by machine learning
arxiv-2110-11618.creator: Sergey Krasikov, Aaron Tranter, Andrey Bogdanov, Yuri Kivshar
arxiv-2110-11618.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Sergey Krasikov, Aaron Tranter, Andrey Bogdanov, Yuri Kivshar. In the recent years, we observe a dramatic boost of research in photonics empowered by the concepts of machine learning and artificial intelligence . The corresponding photonic systems, to which this new methodology is applied, can range from traditional optical waveguides to nanoantennas and metasurfaces, and these novel approaches underpin the fundamental principles of light-matter interaction developed for a smart design of intelligent photonic devices.

arxiv-2209-12953.title: Dialog Acts for Task-Driven Embodied Agents
arxiv-2209-12953.creator: Spandana Gella, Aishwarya Padmakumar, Patrick Lange, Dilek Hakkani-TurAmazon Alexa AI {sgella,padmakua,patlange,hakkanit}@amazon.com
arxiv-2209-12953.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Spandana Gella, Aishwarya Padmakumar, Patrick Lange, Dilek Hakkani-TurAmazon Alexa AI {sgella,padmakua,patlange,hakkanit}@amazon.com. Embodied agents need to be able to interact in natural language – understanding task descriptions and asking appropriate follow up questions to obtain necessary information to be effective at successfully accomplishing tasks for a wide range of users.

arxiv-2211-16518.title: Optimizing sparse fermionic Hamiltonians
arxiv-2211-16518.creator: Yaroslav Herasymenko, Maarten Stroeks, Jonas Helsen, Barbara Terhal
arxiv-2211-16518.description: Abstract We consider the problem of approximating the ground state energy of a fermionic Hamiltonian using a Gaussian state. In sharp contrast to the dense case [ 1 , 2 ] , we prove that strictly q q -local sparse fermionic Hamiltonians have a constant Gaussian approximation ratio; the result holds for any connectivity and interaction strengths.

arxiv-2307-06335.title: Neural Free-Viewpoint Relighting for Glossy Indirect Illumination Volume: 42 Issue: 4
arxiv-2307-06335.creator: Nithin Raghavan, 1∗ Yan Xiao, 1∗ Kai-En Lin, 1 Tiancheng Sun, 2 Sai Bi, 3 Zexiang Xu, 3 Tzu-Mao Li, 1 Ravi Ramamoorthi 1 1 University of California, San Diego 2 Google 3 Adobe Research ∗ denotes equal contribution
arxiv-2307-06335.description: Abstract Precomputed Radiance Transfer (PRT) remains an attractive solution for real-time rendering of complex light transport effects such as glossy global illumination. After precomputation, we can relight the scene with new environment maps while changing viewpoint in real-time. However, practical PRT methods are usually limited to low-frequency spherical harmonic lighting.

arxiv-2402-09509.title: SN 2022jli: The ultraluminous birth of a low-mass X-ray binary Preprint: J.-P. Lasota
arxiv-2402-09509.creator: Andrew King, Jean–Pierre Lasota
arxiv-2402-09509.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Andrew King, Jean–Pierre Lasota. Observations show that the 12.4 d binary system descending from the recent supernova SN 2022jli closely fits hypotheses of how low-mass X-ray binaries form, but requires an apparently super-Eddington accretion luminosity from the accreting component. We show that this agrees very well with the type of accretion-induced beaming found in ultraluminous X-ray sources, as recently strongly confirmed by X-ray polarimetry of the X-ray binary Cyg X-3.

arxiv-2411-15108.title: Pseudo-FIMP dark matter in presence of a SIMP
arxiv-2411-15108.creator: Subhaditya Bhattacharya, Dipankar Pradhan, Jahaan Thakkar
arxiv-2411-15108.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Subhaditya Bhattacharya, Dipankar Pradhan, Jahaan Thakkar. Pseudo-feebly Interacting Massive Particle (pFIMP) has been postulated in two component dark matter (DM) scenarios, where it has feeble interaction with the visible sector, but sizeable one with a thermal bath partner. In this work, we study the possibility and dynamics of pFIMP in presence of a Strongly Interacting Massive Particle (SIMP), which is well known to solve too-big-to-fail and core-vs-cusp problems.

arxiv-2412-06936.title: Creating a Cooperative AI Policymaking Platform through Open-Source Collaboration
arxiv-2412-06936.creator: Humanity Unleashed
arxiv-2412-06936.description: Abstract Advances in artificial intelligence (AI) present significant risks and opportunities, requiring improved governance to mitigate societal harms and promote equitable benefits. Current incentive structures and regulatory delays may hinder responsible AI development and deployment, particularly in light of the transformative potential of large language models (LLMs).

arxiv-2501-18044.title: Recent open heavy flavor studies for the Electron-Ion Collider
arxiv-2501-18044.description: Abstract The future Electron-Ion Collider (EIC) will operate a series of high-luminosity high-energy electron+proton ( e + p e+p ) and electron+nucleus ( e + A ) collisions to study several fundamental questions in the high energy and nuclear physics field.

arxiv-2509-15106.title: Geometric optimization for quantum communication
arxiv-2509-15106.creator: Chengkai Zhu, Hongyu Mao, Kun Fang, Xin Wang
arxiv-2509-15106.description: Abstract Determining the ultimate limits of quantum communication, such as the quantum capacity of a channel and the distillable entanglement of a shared state, remains a central challenge in quantum information theory, primarily due to the phenomenon of superadditivity. This work develops Riemannian optimization methods to establish significantly tighter, computable two-sided bounds on these fundamental quantities.

arxiv-2511-02219.title: TabDSR : Decompose, Sanitize, and Reason for Complex Numerical Reasoning in Tabular Data
arxiv-2511-02219.creator: Changjiang Jiang, Fengchang Yu, Haihua Chen, Wei Lu, Jin Zeng
arxiv-2511-02219.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Changjiang Jiang, Fengchang Yu, Haihua Chen, Wei Lu, Jin Zeng. Complex reasoning over tabular data is crucial in real-world data analysis, yet large language models (LLMs) often underperform due to complex queries, noisy data, and limited numerical capabilities.

arxiv-2511-09333.title: Dual Weighted Residual-driven adaptive mesh refinement to enhance biomechanical simulations
arxiv-2511-09333.creator: Roland Becker, Franz Chouly, Michel Duprez, Thomas Richter, Pierre-Yves Rohan, Thomas Wick
arxiv-2511-09333.description: Abstract This chapter describes how a posteriori error estimates targeting a user-defined quantity of interest, using the Dual Weighted Residual (DWR) technique, can be easily applied for biomechanical simulations in current engineering practice. The proposed method considers a very general setting that encompasses complex geometries, model non-linearities (hyperelasticity, fluid-structure interaction) and multi-goal oriented techniques.

arxiv-2601-00406.title: Large-party limit of topological entanglement entropy in Chern-Simons theory
arxiv-2601-00406.creator: Simran Sain and Siddharth Dwivedi Department of Physics, School of Physical Sciences, Central University of Rajasthan, Ajmer, 305817, India
arxiv-2601-00406.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Simran Sain and Siddharth Dwivedi Department of Physics, School of Physical Sciences, Central University of Rajasthan, Ajmer, 305817, India. plos-pone-0010703.description: PLOS ONE research article. While most of these have been mapped genetically, many remain anonymous. The mutation in the N. crassa temperature-sensitive lethal mut

pmc-10535121.title: The High-Risk Human Papillomavirus Type Influences the Tissue Microenvironment in Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia Grade 2
pmc-10535121.creator: Mayumi Saito, Aarthi Rajesh, Carrie Innes, Rachael van der Griend, Peter Fitzgerald, Bryony Simcock, Peter Sykes, Merilyn Hibma, Jiafen Hu, Vivien Béziat
pmc-10535121.description: High-risk, cancer-causing human papillomavirus (HPV) types are associated with cervical precancer and cancer. A high proportion of high-risk HPV precancer lesions undergo immune-mediated regression. The purpose of this study was to determine if the tissue microenvironment of HPV16 and 18 (HPV16/18) cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 lesions differed from other high-risk types (HPV ‘other’).

pmc-11442536.title: Phosphorus dynamics in volcanic soils of Weizhou Island, China: implications for environmental and agricultural applications
pmc-11442536.creator: Ran Bi, Wei Fu, Xuanni Fu
pmc-11442536.description: The dynamics of phosphorus are intricately governed by geological and ecological processes. Examining phosphorus dynamics in volcanic islands can enhance our comprehension of its behavior within such unique geological systems. However, research on phosphorus dynamics in volcanic islands remains limited.

pmc-11478029.title: Advanced Predictive Modeling of Concrete Compressive Strength and Slump Characteristics: A Comparative Evaluation of BPNN, SVM, and RF Models Optimized via PSO
pmc-11478029.creator: Xuefei Chen, Xiucheng Zhang, Wei-Zhi Chen, Stefano Mariani
pmc-11478029.description: This study presents the development of predictive models for concrete performance, specifically targeting the compressive strength and slump value, utilizing the quantities of individual raw materials in the concrete mix design as input variables. Three distinct machine learning approaches—Backpropagation Neural Network (BPNN), Support Vector Machine (SVM), and Random Forest (RF)—were employed to establish the prediction models independently.

pmc-11586540.creator: Margaret L. Musser, Pamela D. Jones, Teresa L. Goodson, Erin Roof, Chad M. Johannes
pmc-11586540.description: BackgroundInformation regarding response rate to tigilanol tiglate for mast cell tumors in dogs is limited.ObjectivesReport the response rate and durability of tigilanol tiglate intratumoral treatment in dogs with mast cell tumors presented to veterinary oncologists.AnimalsOne hundred forty‐nine dogs; 151 individual tumors.MethodsMulticenter, retrospective survey‐based study.

pmc-11614999.title: Genetically Proxied Therapeutic Effect of Lipid-Lowering Drugs Use, Breast Cancer, and Endometrial Cancer’s Risk: A Drug Target-Based Mendelian Randomization Study
pmc-11614999.creator: Chunxiao Dang, Xiaofeng Wang, Pengfei Liu, Jinxing Liu, Xiao Yu
pmc-11614999.description: BackgroundObservational studies have investigated the association between lipid-lowering drugs and breast cancer (BC) and endometrial cancer (EC), but some controversy remains.ObjectiveThis paper aims to explore the causal relationship between genetic proxies for lipid-lowering drugs and breast and endometrial cancers using drug-target Mendelian randomization (MR).

pmc-11728788.title: Active Vitamin D Ameliorates Arsenite-Induced Thyroid Dysfunction in Sprague–Dawley Rats by Inhibiting the Toll-like Receptor 4/NF-KappaB-Mediated Inflammatory Response
pmc-11728788.creator: Hui Li, Jie Xiang, Qian Song, Ying Jin, Meitong Zhou, Lili Fan, Dapeng Wang
pmc-11728788.description: Arsenic, a well-known environmental endocrine disruptor, exerts interference on the body’s endocrine system. Our previous investigations have demonstrated that chronic exposure to sodium arsenite (NaAsO2) can induce thyroid damage and dysfunction in Sprague–Dawley (SD) rats. Vitamin D (VD) is an indispensable fat-soluble vitamin that plays a crucial role in maintaining thyroid health.

pmc-12437218.title: Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder and Myoclonic Movements Following Streptococcal Pharyngitis: A Rare Pediatric Neuropsychiatric Case
pmc-12437218.creator: J P Carrasco Picazo, J Esteve, C Conde-Pumpido, B Herraiz
pmc-12437218.description: IntroductionPediatric Autoimmune Neuropsychiatric Disorders Associated with Streptococcal infections (PANDAS) typically describe the sudden onset of neuropsychiatric symptoms, such as Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (OCD), following streptococcal infections. However, cases that present with comorbid motor abnormalities, such as myoclonic jerks, are rare and pose diagnostic challenges.

pmc-13006563.title: Analysis of intellectual property strategies across different categories of digital therapeutics
pmc-13006563.creator: Tomoki Maeda, Hiroshi Suzuki, Chikako Saotome
pmc-13006563.description: Advances in digital technology and the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic have accelerated the digital transformation of healthcare. Digital therapeutics (DTx), which deliver evidence-based interventions through digital means to treat or prevent diseases, are expected to generate significant value in modern healthcare.

However, distal emboli and incomplete reperfusion after mechanical thrombectomy are still shortcomings in the care of patients with endovascular acute ischemic stroke. The NeVa NET 5.

pmc-13302539.title: Conduction system pacing restores interpretability and diagnostic performance of exercise stress ECG in patients with prior left bundle branch block: a single-centre pilot study
pmc-13302539.creator: K Shah, C James, H Rutzen-Lopez, V Perez
pmc-13302539.description: Background/IntroductionIn patients with left bundle branch block (LBBB), abnormal septal activation produces baseline ST-segment abnormalities and perfusion artefacts, rendering exercise ECG uninterpretable for ischaemia detection. Current guidelines therefore recommend vasodilator stress imaging or dobutamine stress echocardiography. Conduction system pacing (CSP), using His-bundle or left bundle branch area capture, restores near-physiological ventricular activation.
